newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks rise slightly in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rise slightly in thin market.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London rose slightly in quiet trading on Monday, with the holiday in Hong Kong creating a moribund market.

London's Hang Seng London Reference Index tracked the UK's FTSE-100 to rise 30.03 points to 12,540.08 by 1501 GMT. In Hong Kong, the market was closed for the Chung Yeung holiday, after closing on Friday at the record level of 12,510.05.
Traders said the market was thin, with most stocks unchanged and little movement elsewhere. Yet shares are expected to continue on their upward trend after the holiday.
"The market needed to take a bit of a breather before surging higher," said one trader.
In London HSBC shares rose to HK$156.1 by 1415 GMT, HK$1.1 above their HK$155.0 close in Hong Kong on Friday. Cathay Pacific shares rose to HK$12.625 after closing at HK$12.6 in Hong Kong.
